ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of every director, officer, shareholder holding at least 25% control, and authorized signatory against FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) guidance, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, Canada's autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the Criminal Code terrorist listing regime, and the Justice Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence is required where the shareholder is a non-resident corporation, a state-owned enterprise, or a person connected with jurisdictions subject to FATF monitoring. A documented screening log, risk rating, and evidentiary record must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship for FINTRAC audit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online via https://www.bcregistries.gov.bc.ca); optional federal name clearance through Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre at https://www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/cc/CorporationsCanada/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: British Columbia corporate names must be in English or French or must include a Latin-alphabet transliteration that is registered as the primary legal name. Names consisting wholly of non-Latin script are not accepted as the statutory corporate name; a foreign-language e-bike brand name may be protected through a transliterated additional name or trade-mark only. The legal name must contain a distinctive element plus a legal element such as 'Ltd.', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', or 'BC Ltd.' and must not be otherwise misleading or confusing with an existing BC or federal corporate name or registered trade-mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed corporate name is refused, the applicant may within 30 days of written rejection submit a formal request for reconsideration to the BC Registrar through BC Registries and Online Services, attaching search results, evidence of consent from the rights holder, and written legal submissions demonstrating the name is not deceptively misleading. If reconsideration fails, the applicant may either select a new distinctive name or incorporate using the BC incorporation-number designation and subsequently register a trade name. A final refusal that affects a legal right may be challenged by judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act; practical alternative is to re-file under the federal Corporations Canada procedure where the name is federally clearable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only where the provider is a licensed British Columbia registered agent maintaining a physical street address in the province and accepts service of process. A purely virtual 'mail-forwarding only' address is not compliant. For this manufacturing and import/export operation, a registered agent's physical office will satisfy the statutory registered office and records office requirements if it includes the statutory records address. The actual manufacturing, warehousing, and operational footprint may be located elsewhere in or outside BC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (estimated 20-25% likelihood in the first three years) due to the import-heavy micro-mobility OEM profile. Unannounced corporate registry inspections are uncommon, but Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), provincial consumer product safety authorities, and FINTRAC document-based AML compliance audits may occur; an actual physical on-site inspection of the registered office is unlikely absent a tax, sanctions, or regulatory trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (British Columbia) — ss. 3-22 (incorporation), s. 51 (shares), s. 198 (registered office), s. 133 (restoration on default)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) together with Incorporation Agreement (Form 2) filed via BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account is required. The BC Act expressly permits incorporation with zero or nominal capital, and directors may determine the consideration for issued shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Board ratifies the subscriber share allotment set out in the Incorporation Agreement and confirms the class, voting rights, and issue price of all issued shares. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Company shall be established at [registered address], British Columbia, and the Corporate Registry records agent be designated accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Name] be appointed President & CEO, [Name] be appointed Corporate Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Chief Financial Officer, each with authority to open corporate bank accounts, sign banking resolutions, and execute routine operational agreements. RESOLVED FINALLY THAT any one director or officer be and is hereby authorized to file all post-incorporation documents with BC Registries, the Canada Revenue Agency, and WorkSafeBC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry via Corporate Online (CORES), Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Approval Request through the Corporate Online portal, providing the proposed name in the mandatory BC format (Distinctive Element + Descriptive Element + Legal Element, e.g., Pacific Cargo E-Bike Manufacturing Ltd.). The name must not be identical to an existing BC or extra-provincial registration and must not contravene the Business Corporations Act name restrictions. A NUANS-style search within BC is automatically performed by the registries system; the result shall be reserved for 56 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised Name Approval Request within the reservation window, or apply to the Registrar for discretionary approval with a supporting statutory declaration explaining the use and distinctiveness of the proposed name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry (declarations filed by incorporators)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Incorporation Agreement (Form 2) and Notice of Articles (Form 1) in prescribed BC registry formats. Each incorporator must execute the Incorporation Agreement indicating the number and class of shares taken. The Notice of Articles must specify the registered office address (physical street address in British Columbia), the directors, and the authorized share structure, including the new BC requirement to disclose the duration of the corporation, if any. Verify that at least one director is a Canadian resident as required under the Business Corporations Act.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Agreement (Form 2) signed by all incorporators
Actual registered office address in BC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the documents contain a deficiency, the Registry issues a Notice of Objection; the incorporator must resubmit corrected forms with a Letter of Explanation. Rejected applications are returnable without prejudice within 30 days, and fees are generally refundable or transferable to the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with BC Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the BC Corporate Online portal, enter the Name Approval reference and the data from the Notice of Articles and Incorporation Agreement, pay the CAD 350 statutory filing fee by credit card or debit, and electronically transmit the completed application. The system performs automated validation against duplicate names and statutory compliance; the Certificate of Incorporation is issued upon successful payment and validation.
required_dossiers: Credit card or bank debit authorization for fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic filing is rejected or queried, the filing client can correct the validation errors and resubmit the same business day. A formal appeal of systemic rejection may be addressed to the Registrar by way of a Request for Review accompanied by the original Notice of Objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (automated system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful filing, the system issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation containing the registration number and the date of incorporation. The incorporators or first directors must then ratify the organizational resolutions: issue share certificates to subscribers, adopt the corporate seal (optional), create the share register, register the registered office designation, and minute the appointment of officers as approved by the First Board Resolution.
required_dossiers: Share certificates issued per share class
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is issued with a clerical error, the company may file a Clerk's Notice of Error under section 35 of the Business Corporations Act within 60 days seeking administrative correction from the Registry without court involvement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registration with Revenue, Occupational Insurance, and Municipal Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Provincial Sales Tax (PST) branch of the BC Ministry of Finance, WorkSafeBC, and the local municipal licencing division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) with sub-accounts for Corporate Income Tax, GST/HST (mandatory for manufacturing sales), and Payroll Deductions. Register separately for BC PST (7%) as a selling manufacturer, register with WorkSafeBC for workers' compensation assessment and occupational safety coverage, and apply to the relevant municipal jurisdiction (e.g., City of Surrey or City of Vancouver) for a Business Licence classified under manufacturing and assembly of transportation equipment.
required_dossiers: Business licence application with lease evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For CRA or PST registration discrepancies, file an RC1 adjustment request within 90 days. For municipal licence delays, a temporary occupancy permit may be obtained pending full licence issuance, subject to compliance with zoning. WorkSafeBC objections are cured by submitting payroll estimates and confirming a written occupational health and safety program.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal licensing board (e.g., City of Surrey Business Licensing Division) in coordination with the BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (Environmental Management Act) and WorkSafeBC
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (Manufacturing & Light Assembly, NAICS 336991) and WorkSafeBC Firm Registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (Environmental Assessment Office and regional environmental protection branch)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Standard Permitting — no Full EIA Report required for urban electric cargo bicycle assembly under the Environmental Assessment Act, unless the project includes large-scale metal finishing, powder coating, or battery pack manufacturing exceeding air emission thresholds (VOCs > 10 tonnes per year), which would trigger an environmental management permit under the Environmental Management Act
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to sewer: pH 6.0-9.5, total suspended solids < 50 mg/L, oil and grease < 15 mg/L, and no free petroleum hydrocarbons; VOC emissions from painting/powder-coating booths must be captured with controlled filtration achieving 85% or higher destruction efficiency; any lithium-ion battery electrolyte, acid, or solvent waste must be handled as dangerous waste under BC Hazardous Waste Regulation (B.C. Reg. 63/88), stored in sealed containers, and transported by a licensed carrier

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for industrial occupancy from the local fire marshal, including spray booth and lithium battery storage compliance with the BC Fire Code (sprinkler protection required for storage areas over threshold volume); structural load inspection confirming floor loading capacity for forklift traffic and battery palletizing; WorkSafeBC occupational clearance issued only after completion of a site-specific health and safety orientation, emergency evacuation plan approval, and confirmation of proper grounding for all electrical charging stations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and corporate income tax; British Columbia Ministry of Finance for BC PST. Official portals: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html and eTaxBC tax.gov.bc.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must apply to the CRA for a 15-digit Business Number (BN) and relevant Programme Accounts (RT, RP, RC, RM) using Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1. Required documentation includes certified articles of incorporation/registration, registered office address, director/officer particulars, and a completed non-resident tax form (Form RC459 or equivalent) when applicable. BC PST registration is then completed through the BC eTaxBC portal using the BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election under Canadian domestic law. A Canadian incorporated corporation is a separate taxpayer; small business deduction eligibility requires Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) status. GST/HST related corporations can elect to file as a single registrant (Section 156 election); non-residents may make a Section 216 election for net-basis taxation on Canadian rental property income. Provincial income tax is collected by CRA under the Tax Collection Agreement with no separate provincial election for BC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) at 7% (dual indirect tax system)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated) per any 12 consecutive calendar quarters; for BC PST: immediate registration required upon carrying on business in BC with no simplified low-revenue threshold, including for non-resident vendors with a physical or substantial presence.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls (CTC). The CRA accepts electronic records and supports compliant EDI/API transmission; BC PST requires prescribed sales invoices and detailed records but has no prior-approval clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, Part V, Section 1 for tangible personal property (electric cargo e-bikes) supplied by a commercial manufacturer and exported by the supplier or a customer acting as agent, provided the goods are physically delivered outside Canada within the required time frames and the supplier maintains documentary evidence establishing export. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated when performed wholly outside Canada and no benefit is conferred inside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency B13A Export Declaration (customs export declaration)
Bill of Lading or through-waybill naming a consignee outside Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank evidence of foreign currency proceeds repatriated to Canada)
Commercial invoice issued to the non-resident purchaser with zero-rating indicator
Packing list showing export marks, HS classification, and country of origin
Transport and delivery evidence (marine/air/land) including proof of arrival at foreign destination
CBSA or logistics custodian certification of export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA can deny the zero-rating and claw back GST/HST net tax, input tax credits, and refunds when export evidence is deficient; normal reassessment period is four years after the return, extended to the later of six/ten years or indefinitely for misrepresentation. Civil penalties include the Excise Tax Act s.280 false representation penalty (24% of the stated amount), s.285 gross negligence penalty (50% of the net tax amount), and s.288 recapture of input tax credits. Criminal sanctions for willful evasion under ETA s.327-329 include fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. Exporters must retain all substantiating records for at least six years (BC PST records: five years) and face summary dismissal of any contested claim without the mandatory export bundle.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with regulatory perimeter shared by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank supervision, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF and cross-border wire reporting, and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) for inbound investment review under the Investment Canada Act. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign exchange administration; exchange liberalization is the statutory norm and the Minister of Finance retains macro-financial oversight under the Bank of Canada Act and the Financial Administration Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full free convertibility on both current account and capital account. The Canadian dollar is an independently floating major reserve currency with no exchange-control permits, quotas, approval gates, or repatriation requirements. Trade payments, dividends, royalties, intercompany settlements, and direct equity injections move freely without prior authorization. The only material frictions are (i) Part XIII withholding tax of 25% on dividends and certain payments to non-residents, reduced to 5% or 15% under applicable income tax treaties for corporate shareholders holding at least 10% voting power; (ii) FINTRAC international electronic funds transfer (ETF) reporting for every cross-border wire of C$10,000 or more; and (iii) transfer-pricing and thin-capitalization limits under ITA sections 247 and 18(4), which cap deductible interest on shareholder debt at a 1.5:1 debt-to-equity ratio.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export receipts. A BC corporation may retain USD or third-currency proceeds indefinitely in domestic or offshore accounts. Compliance is confined to (i) filing electronic export declarations with the Canada Border Services Agency through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for commercial goods valued at C$2,000 or more per shipment, using HS 8711.60 for electric cargo bicycles with auxiliary electric motor and HS 8711.90 for other cycles; (ii) maintaining statutory books and CRA income recognition for export revenue; (iii) executing a USMCA Certificate of Origin for United States-bound shipments; and (iv) accepting automatic FINTRAC reporting by the bank for any international EFT of C$10,000 or more.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a supplementary settlement rail; Low as a primary treasury substitute. A foreign or domestic EMI operating in Canada must register as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and, if carrying on business in British Columbia, obtain registration under the BC Money Services Act. EMIs are not deposit-taking institutions under the federal Bank Act, cannot issue documentary letters of credit, do not have direct access to Payments Canada settlement systems (Lynx and Real-Time Rail), and funds held with them are not CDIC-insured. The commercially legal architecture is hybrid: (i) a Tier-1 Schedule I bank account for equity injections, LC-backed component imports, CAD payroll, and CRA remittances; (ii) an EMI wallet such as Wise Business or Airwallex used strictly for low-value collection concentration from fragmented wholesale and direct-to-consumer orders; and (iii) systematic sweeps from the EMI wallet to the Tier-1 account with full transaction-level evidence. The OEM itself does not become an MSB by merely receiving EMI transfers and requires no MSB licence provided it does not provide money remittance services to third parties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian federal and British Columbia law do not mandate physical attendance of directors at the bank branch. FINTRAC client identification rules permit non-face-to-face verification through approved dual-process digital ID solutions or credit-file cross-checks, supplemented by a bank-conducted video interview. In practice, RBC, TD, BMO, and CIBC will onboard a BC-incorporated company fully remotely when at least one director is a Canadian resident and the ultimate beneficial owner is identified through the corporate transparency register. A foreign-resident director or UBO holding 25% or more must provide a certified passport copy, a banker's reference from the home institution, and a video confirmation; the bank may condition account activation on a physical visit by the primary signing officer, particularly before issuing corporate credit cards or USD clearing limits. A CBCA or BC-registered corporation should present the Notice of Articles, Articles of Incorporation, directors' resolution, and register of directors at opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fresh incorporation (under 24 months) receiving the first inbound equity wire from a foreign parent in a jurisdiction on the FATF monitoring list, combined with an ultimate beneficial owner who is not a Canadian resident.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Short-form incorporation records including Articles and Notice of Articles; register of directors and share register; executed share subscription agreement; board resolution authorizing the account and the capital contribution; the foreign parent's certificate of good standing; source-of-funds confirmation from the foreign parent's own bank; percentage breakdown of all UBOs with certified identification; organizational chart; and a Canadian counsel opinion confirming the transaction has no money-laundering or sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export sales invoices settled by wires from a third-party remitter whose name does not match the contractual buyer, which is a layering red flag in trade transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-party payment direction letter signed by the buyer, the seller, and the remitter; amended commercial invoices and packing lists; signed purchase orders; bill of lading or air waybill; CBSA CERS export declarations; USMCA Certificate of Origin for US-bound cargo; remitter bank statements; agency or consolidator agreement explaining the payment chain; and written explanation of the commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentrated large prepayments on component imports from suppliers domiciled in non-AEOI or high-risk trade corridors, particularly when prepayment terms exceed 60 days and no documentary credit is used.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier master contract and current purchase orders; commercial invoices and thermographic packing lists; confirmation of the underlying SWIFT MT103; cargo and marine insurance certificates; customs entry evidence on the Canadian side; OECD-transfer-pricing-compliant documentation demonstrating arm's length pricing of any related-party prepayments; and a cash-flow rationale memo supporting the prepayment terms as a supply-chain security measure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (i) The foreign parent remits via SWIFT MT103 strictly from its own bank account, with the beneficiary being the BC corporation; the remittance information field must read 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - [corporate name] - [allotment reference]'; personal accounts of directors, third-party nominees, or commingled funding must never be used. (ii) For USD funding, the Canadian bank will accept MT103 through its US clearing correspondent (CHIPS/Fedwire) with onward book transfer into the corporation's USD-denominated operational account; no Canadian 'purpose code' is required by banks, although narrative remittance references must align with the underlying allotment to satisfy the bank's FINTRAC international-EFT report for wires of C$10,000 or more. (iii) Corporate housekeeping must be simultaneous: allot shares in accordance with the BC Business Corporations Act or the federal CBCA, file the share structure update in the BC corporate registry, and execute share certificates held in the corporate minute book; a federal corporation must file the change with Corporations Canada. (iv) Tax treatment: an equity injection is non-taxable and is not subject to Part XIII withholding; if funds arrive as intercompany shareholder debt, the corporation must apply arm's length interest, respect the 1.5:1 thin-cap ratio, and file CRA Form T106 when non-arm's length transactions exceed C$1,000,000 in the year; later dividend remittances to a treaty-resident parent carry Part XIII at the applicable treaty rate. (v) Investment Canada Act: establishment of a new Canadian business by a non-Canadian below the multi-billion-dollar WTO direct-acquisition threshold requires no pre-closing review; only a short-form notification is considered, and for a de novo BC manufacturing subsidiary the transaction is outside review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Rails available to the BC OEM: (i) Domestic CAD high-value payments execute through Payments Canada Lynx (RTGS) initiated from the Tier-1 treasury portal, and operational low-value payments through the Real-Time Rail (RTR) where posted payment-size limits apply; (ii) cross-border USD disbursements for battery cells, motors, controllers, and frame components are cleared by SWIFT MT103 through CHIPS or Fedwire with the bank's nostro relationships; (iii) trade finance settlements use an irrevocable commercial documentary letter of credit compliant with UCP600, issued via SWIFT MT700 where suppliers require bank payment security, or a deferred-payment LC for repeat suppliers; standby LCs and documentary collections (MT400/MT500) are available for performance and collections; (iv) CAD-USD conversion is executed on the bank's daily FX desk or via pre-negotiated forward cover; (v) for US dealer receivables, the exporter may use a USD concentration account, cross-border receivables discounting, or forfaiting, provided full invoice, bill of lading, and customs entry evidence is retained for each drawdown.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable plain-vanilla FX forwards with a licensed Schedule I bank, covering CAD/USD and CAD/CNH tenors up to 12 months, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or single-transaction treasury confirmations; no exchange-control approval is required for a BC manufacturing company with transactional exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in currencies without a fully accessible onshore deliverable market (notably offshore CNH, KRW, or INR) used strictly to hedge identified commercial exposures; these are permissible when booked with an approved derivatives dealer and must respect OSFI margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives, including variation margin mechanics imposed on the bank counterparty.

Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps aligning USD import payables with CAD functional-currency cash flows, entered under ISDA terms and limited to balance-sheet hedging, supported by a board-approved FX risk policy containing an explicit no-speculation mandate; the end-user hedging exemption applies to the corporation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined: 15% federal (s. 123(1)(a) ITA) + 12% British Columbia general corporate income tax rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal M&P profits deduction reducing the federal rate to 13% for qualified manufacturing profits (combined BC M&P 25%); 15% non-refundable SR&ED investment tax credit (35% refundable for CCPCs); Accelerated Investment Incentive and immediate expensing for Class 43 manufacturing machinery; general rate for large corporations is not subject to the CCPC small business deduction (federal 9%/BC 2% available only to CCPCs controlled by Canadian residents).
